problem: Let $b=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 30 \\ 12 \\ 24\end{aligned}]$ and $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto $\text{Span}{a}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector onto a One-Dimensional Subspace
examples.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066555/assets/8a460dfb89b0d2e9c1e197aa212f494971df1c36822117fb4b1271f5608d1d1a.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066555/assets/a172f54b0dc879c2363cfd2818fc79614d68662def6dd56b0ac9aec8fdbca1a5.png) Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{b}\}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{b\cdot a}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 2+1\cdot 9+0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{4+9+0-1}{4+1+0+1}b \\  & =\frac{12}{6}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
